title: Elastic-net analysis links positive self-processing with reward motivation in depression
summary: Elastic-net models compared cognitive and physiological predictors of self-reported reward responsivity and approach motivation in 202 young adults spanning depression severity. Positive self-referential processing was the most robust, modest predictor; held-out variance explained ranged from 5.0–12.2% for approach motivation and 9.7–28.0% for reward responsivity. Nested cross-validation and a repeat assessment supported prediction within this restricted sample. These observational associations do not establish causal direction or an effective intervention.
organization: Georgetown University Medical Center; University of Texas at Austin

source_review.scope: Primary full article Methods, Results and limitations plus Europe PMC bibliographic metadata; PMC full article.

evidence.tested: Held-out prediction and one-week repeat assessment of self-reported reward-related measures.
evidence.unknown: Causal direction, intervention benefit and transportability beyond the restricted young-adult sample remain unestablished.
evidence.ai_role: Elastic-net lasso/ridge penalties select correlated cognitive predictors; nested tuning within ten-fold cross-validation repeated ten times. Time-two assessment uses current time-two predictors, not forecasting an intervention effect.
